verification_levels.abstract_verified: The quoted statement appears in the PubMed abstract retrieved in this session (2026-11-01, PubMed MCP).
verification_levels.recalled_not_reread: Value recalled from the cited work; the page was NOT re-read in this session. Treated as a wide prior, never as a point value.
verification_levels.repo_pinned: Value read from a file already committed in this repository (path + sha256 in the run receipt).
verification_levels.assumption: Engineering assumption with no source; swept or flagged.

preuss2006.cite: Preuss T et al. 2006 J Neurosci 26:3454-64
preuss2006.used: Looming-evoked C-starts in goldfish: response probability 0.70-0.91; mean latency from looming onset 142-716 ms; M-cell is the threshold detector; threshold tracks a dynamically scaled function of angular image size.
preuss2006.quote: response probabilities between 0.7 and 0.91 and mean latencies ranging from 142 to 716 ms

eaton2001.cite: Eaton RC, Lee RK, Foreman MB 2001 Prog Neurobiol 63:467-85
eaton2001.used: M-cell as command-like neuron feeding a lower-level CPG; stimulus approach angle sets the timing/magnitude of agonist/antagonist contractions and the escape trajectory.

domenici_blake1997.cite: Domenici P, Blake RW 1997 J Exp Biol 200:1165-78
domenici_blake1997.used: Fast-start stage structure and wide priors: Mauthner-mediated (short) latency ~5-15 ms after an abrupt (mechano-acoustic) stimulus; stage-1 duration ~10-40 ms increasing with size; peak turning rates of order 10^3-10^4 deg/s in 5-30 cm fish. Abstract retrieved; numbers not re-read.

domenici_hale2019.cite: Domenici P, Hale ME 2019 J Exp Biol 222:jeb166009
domenici_hale2019.used: C- and S-starts, single vs double bend; context-dependent variability of escape kinematics and neural control (not all-or-none).

domenici2011.cite: Domenici P, Blagburn JM, Bacon JP 2011 J Exp Biol 214:2463-73
domenici2011.used: Away responses 50-90% of the time; escape trajectories mainly 90-180 deg from the threat, often multimodal.
domenici2011.quote: away responses occur only approximately 50-90% of the time ... mainly 90-180 deg away from the threat

burgess_granato2007.cite: Burgess HA, Granato M 2007 J Neurosci 27:4984-94
burgess_granato2007.used: Larval zebrafish acoustic startle: short-latency C-starts (Mauthner-dependent, ~5 ms) versus long-latency C-starts (~tens of ms). Abstract retrieved (PPI context); latency numbers not re-read.

park_choi2010.cite: Park H, Choi H 2010 J Exp Biol 213:3269-79
park_choi2010.used: Cypselurus hiraii models: max L/D near 0 deg attack; CL largest at 30-35 deg attack, the angle at which flying fish are observed to emerge; pelvic fins raise L/D and longitudinal static stability; ground effect reduces drag.
park_choi2010.quote: The lift coefficient is largest at attack angles around 30~35 deg, at which the flying fish is observed to emerge from the sea surface

saro_cortes2022.cite: Saro-Cortes V et al. 2022 Integr Comp Biol
saro_cortes2022.used: Robotic flying-fish model at Re 30,000: pelvic fins directly behind pectorals maximise efficiency; pitching stability is not achievable for positive pelvic pitch angles nor for pelvic fins directly below the pectoral: a stability-vs-lift trade-off.

deng2019.cite: Deng J et al. 2019 Bioinspir Biomim 14:046009
deng2019.used: CFD of a C. hiraii-like model: CL_max 1.03; max L/D 4.7; longitudinally stable for appropriate CG (negative Cm slope).

taylor2003.cite: Taylor GK, Nudds RL, Thomas ALR 2003 Nature 425:707-11
taylor2003.used: Cruising swimmers and fliers use 0.2 < St < 0.4 (St = fA/U); used as a plausibility band, not a constraint.

wardle1975.used: Maximum tail-beat frequency is limited by the minimum muscle contraction time (one twitch per half-beat), which grows with body size and falls with temperature. No abstract in PubMed; used only to justify sweeping a muscle corner frequency 20-70 Hz.

ijspeert2007.used: Oscillator form already implemented in engineering/behavior/model.py (reused unchanged, imported).

ehrlich_schoppik2017.cite: Ehrlich DE, Schoppik D 2017 Curr Biol 27:334-44
ehrlich_schoppik2017.used: Larval zebrafish are constantly destabilised in pitch and correct posture by timing swim bouts (vestibular-driven balance); motivates an intermittent/bout controller as an alternative to continuous fin servoing.

fish1990.cite: Fish FE 1990 Copeia 1990(2):390-7 (Wing design and scaling of flying fish)
fish1990.used: Taxi speed rise 10 -> 16-20 m/s (p.397 citing Shoulejkin), as already cited in engineering/simulation/controlled.py RELEASE_SPEEDS. Allometric Cypselurus fit used by the organism glide baseline.

lighthill1971.cite: Lighthill MJ 1971 Proc R Soc Lond B 179:125-38 (Large-amplitude elongated-body theory of fish locomotion)
lighthill1971.used: Mean reactive thrust T = (m_a/2)[<h_t^2> - U^2 <h_x^2>] at the trailing edge, m_a = (pi/4) rho s^2; derived in caudal_cpg.py and checked numerically.

edgerton_breder1941.cite: Edgerton HE, Breder CM 1941 Zoologica 26:311-4 (High-speed photographs of flying fishes in flight)
edgerton_breder1941.used: Taxiing tail-beat frequencies reported of order 50-70 Hz (as summarised in later reviews). Not in PubMed; used only as the upper end of a swept range.
